speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Could you tell me when these symptoms of double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness first started, and have they been getting worse throughout the day?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually occurs when I look up or down, but not when I look straight ahead. The weakness in my arms and legs feels worse after climbing stairs or doing other activities, but it gets better if I rest for a while. I have not noticed any changes in balance or coordination, and I do not have tingling or numbness, just the weakness and fatigue.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, so the symptoms fluctuate with activity and improve with rest. Do you experience any difficulty swallowing, slurred speech, or changes in your facial muscles?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not noticed any issues with eye tracking or movement when looking straight ahead. I have not had any recent infections or fevers, and I do not have a family history of neurological disorders. The weakness feels symmetrical, affecting both arms and both legs equally.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any drooping of your eyelids, especially later in the day or after prolonged activity? Given your symptom pattern, I would like to request some specific tests. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody. REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 36.6°C (97.9°F), Blood Pressure 125/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 72 bpm, Respiratory Rate 16 breaths/min. Neurological Examination: Cranial Nerves show presence of ptosis (drooping of the right upper eyelid) that worsens with sustained upward gaze; Motor Strength is diminished in the upper extremities with normal tone and no atrophy; Reflexes and Sensation are normal throughout. Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies: Present (elevated). Electromyography (Repetitive Nerve Stimulation): Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation. Chest CT: Normal, no thymoma or other masses detected.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of ptosis, fluctuating weakness, and positive acetylcholine receptor antibodies confirms your condition. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.
